# Feedback, Verification, and Learning {#sec-feedback-verification-trust}

::: {.epigraph}
> *"Program testing can be used to show the presence of bugs, but never to show their absence!"*
>
> — Edsger W. Dijkstra, *Notes on Structured Programming* (1970) [@Dijkstra1970Notes]
:::

::: {.column-margin}
**Author's note.** Dijkstra's warning separates a check from the stronger claim
someone might attach to it. Passing tests supports only the conditions and
behaviors the tests exercised. A failed test can still decisively contradict a
bounded claim.
:::

::: {.callout-crux}
When does a return from an architecture tool become a usable measurement, what
comparison can it support, and what should the result change?
:::

The tool-connected environment handed forward the intentionally incomplete
Lighthouse cache record in @tbl-lighthouse-execution-record. It reports SRAM
and cycle-level returns for the 2, 3, and 4\ MB candidates, one stale-state
attempt, two later clean 3\ MB attempts, and an exhausted cycle-level budget.

The record also says what is missing. It does not retain exact translated
inputs, tool and model versions, parser status, raw artifact identities, frame
identifiers, reset state, or attempt-level attribution for the aggregate 3\ MB
values. The values came from a constructed teaching example rather than a live
project run. A complete-looking table could hide those limitations, but it
could not repair them.

This is the right place to begin. A returned number is not automatically a
measurement. A measurement is not automatically a valid comparison. A valid
comparison supports only the property, candidate, conditions, and check scope
that produced it. AI makes these distinctions more important because it can
produce and score candidates faster, search directly against imperfect
proxies, and generate explanations that sound more certain than the
measurements allow. It does not change what an architecture result must
contain.

::: {.callout-learning-objectives}
After reading this chapter, you can:

- Distinguish execution status from measurement status and identify the fields
  a returned value needs before it can enter a comparison.
- Build a matched comparison with a named candidate, comparator, quantity,
  unit, conditions, uncertainty, and decision margin.
- State what a formal check, simulation, implementation tool, or physical
  measurement can and cannot establish.
- Diagnose proxy mismatch, confounding, variability, and selection bias before
  treating a reported difference as an architecture result.
- Separate an observed outcome from its proposed mechanism, record nonclaims,
  and route a needed revision to the part of the study that owns it.

:::

## From Tool Return to Measurement {#sec-from-feedback-to-decision}

Execution and interpretation answer different questions. The environment
records whether a request was valid, what ran, what failed, which artifacts
returned, and what state and cost accompanied the attempt. Interpretation asks
whether a returned field measures the requested quantity and whether it can be
compared with another field.

A failed setup is therefore not a poor measurement of a candidate. It is no
candidate measurement at all. A clean process exit may still return a partial
report, omit a required field, use the wrong unit, or parse an unfamiliar
warning as success. A complete return can contain a genuine limit violation.
Execution status must survive intact so interpretation can distinguish these
cases.

The useful sequence is shown in @fig-evidence-flow. Each completed step adds
something the preceding step did not establish. An incomplete measurement can
return directly to execution, and an invalid comparison can return directly to
study formulation.

![**A tool return gains meaning in stages.** The execution record first
supplies a return with status and lineage. Measurement qualification binds a
quantity to a candidate and conditions. A matched comparison adds a
comparator, difference, and uncertainty. A scoped interpretation states what
the result supports and does not support. Qualification failures return to the
environment, comparison failures return to study formulation, and a completed
interpretation records learning and any needed revision.](images/F8-evidence-flow){#fig-evidence-flow
width="88%" fig-alt="A five-step flow from tool return through measurement
qualification and matched comparison to scoped interpretation and
a recorded next step. Side paths send incomplete measurements to the
environment and invalid comparisons to study formulation."}

### Qualifying a Returned Value

A measurement record needs enough information to answer six questions
(@tbl-measurement-record).

| **Field** | **Question the record must answer** |
| --- | --- |
| **Candidate identity** | Which design revision, configuration, software state, and workload produced the value? |
| **Quantity and unit** | What property was measured or computed, how was it aggregated, and in what unit? |
| **Conditions** | Which tool, model, configuration, corner, seed where relevant, and operating conditions apply? |
| **Extraction status** | Did the expected artifact exist, parse under the declared schema, and retain unfamiliar warnings? |
| **Variation and error** | What repetitions, sampling method, numerical tolerance, model error, or known bound limits the value? |
| **Source record** | Which returned artifact and execution attempt support the field, and can the value be recovered from them? |

: **A measurement is a returned value with identity, meaning, conditions, and
limits.** These fields test whether the execution record is sufficient for the
comparison being attempted.
{#tbl-measurement-record tbl-colwidths="[24,76]"}

The environment chapter owns returned artifacts, extraction status, recorded
conditions, and lineage. This chapter does not reconstruct missing versions or
rerun a parser. It owns whether the quantity, aggregation, error, comparator,
and check scope make the returned field usable as a measurement. Missing
execution fields return to the environment. Inadequate observations or an
invalid comparison return to study formulation.

The Lighthouse record demonstrates three interpretation rules. The clean
returns can illustrate comparison logic, but they must be rerun or recovered
before they become independently qualified project measurements. The
stale-state attempt is a setup failure rather than a measurement of the 3\ MB
candidate. The reported absence of a 4\ MB cycle-level call is a scheduling
outcome until retained parser and dispatch evidence verifies the short-circuit.
Missing information remains part of each result.

This distinction prevents two common errors. An infrastructure failure cannot
become negative training data about a design. A favorable value with unknown
conditions cannot become evidence simply because its unit looks familiar.

## Constructing a Valid Comparison {#sec-evidence-specific-to-claim-and-scope}

Architecture decisions usually depend on differences rather than isolated
values. A cache study asks how a candidate differs from a baseline under the
same workload and software state. A method study asks how one proposal process
differs from a credible alternative under the same search and evaluation
budget. The comparator is part of the claim, not a footnote added after the
result.

@fig-claim-frame summarizes the minimum frame. A candidate and comparator feed
one measured difference. Workload and design state, tool conditions,
uncertainty, and check scope bound where that difference applies.

![**A comparison binds two designs to one measured difference and its
limits.** Candidate and comparator are evaluated for the same quantity and
unit. The result remains conditional on workload and state, tool conditions,
uncertainty, and the property the check can observe.](images/F7-claim-frame){#fig-claim-frame
width="100%" fig-alt="Three-column comparison frame. Candidate
and comparator feed a measured quantity, difference, and uncertainty, which
are bounded by workload and design state, tool conditions, and check scope."}

For matched cases \(c_j\), the basic paired difference is

$$
d_j = y(\text{candidate}, c_j) - y(\text{comparator}, c_j).
$$

The sign convention must be stated. Positive may mean improvement for
throughput and regression for latency. A percentage must name its
denominator. An aggregate must state whether it is a mean, percentile, maximum,
geometric mean, or another statistic. Without those choices, two correct
numbers can still form an incoherent comparison.

### Match What Can Change the Result

The candidate and comparator should differ only along the factors the study
intends to compare. Workload, software, model version, tool flags, operating
point, warmup, sampling window, and resource budget can all create a
difference that has nothing to do with the architecture change. A matched
comparison records them rather than relying on similar filenames or a shared
directory.

Systematic model error sometimes cancels in a relative comparison. It does so
only when the model treats the candidate and comparator similarly in the
region being studied. A frozen simulator can support an ordering even when its
absolute prediction differs from silicon, but that bargain fails when the
architecture change crosses an unmodeled boundary or affects one candidate
differently. Cancellation is a hypothesis to check, not a property of using
the same tool.

### Put the Difference Beside Its Uncertainty

Repeated measurements estimate run-to-run variability when the flow or
workload is variable. Paired resampling can preserve the relationship between
matched baseline and candidate frames. Numerical tolerances, finite sampling,
heuristic variation, and model error may require different treatments. One
generic error bar cannot represent all of them.

The Lighthouse walkthrough uses a different stated sign convention for tail
latency. It reports improvement as baseline latency minus candidate latency,
so a positive value means the candidate is faster. Under that convention, the
reported reduction is 0.3\ ms and its illustrative 95% interval runs from
-0.1\ ms to 0.7\ ms, using paired block resampling over matched frame
sequences. Because the interval includes no improvement, the comparison does
not resolve the declared tail-latency question. The point estimate is
favorable, but its uncertainty spans both a small regression and a larger
improvement. The interval cannot be recomputed from the surviving constructed
record because the matched frame identities are missing. It remains an
illustrative reported comparison rather than a replayed calculation.

A decision margin adds a second test. If the study requires an improvement of
at least \(m\), the comparison must resolve the result relative to \(m\), not
merely relative to zero. A difference inside known measurement resolution or
uncertainty remains unresolved. Calling it a tie may be appropriate under a
predeclared rule, but calling it an improvement is not.

### Protect Against Confounding and Selection

A matched comparison can still support the wrong explanation. Confounding
exists when another changed factor could account for the result. Stable
versions, ablations, matched contrasts, and sensitivity studies help separate
the intended change from plausible alternatives.

Selection introduces another problem. If a search evaluates many noisy
candidates and reports only the best, the selected value retains some of the
luck that made it win. Repeating the same search data does not remove that
bias. The chosen candidate should be measured again on fresh seeds, workloads,
or cases that did not select it. The fresh evaluation asks whether the margin
survives after the search has stopped choosing the winner.

## What a Check Can and Cannot Establish {#sec-independent-checks-and-correlated-errors}

A valid measurement may still address the wrong property. Syntax checks,
functional simulation, model checking, performance simulation, synthesis,
timing analysis, power analysis, and post-silicon characterization answer
different questions. Their strength is not a single ordering from weak to
strong. A parser can conclusively reject an illegal request while an expensive
timing run says nothing about functional correctness. @tbl-check-scope gives
representative boundaries rather than a universal ordering.

| **Check class** | **What it can support within stated conditions** | **What it does not establish by itself** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Syntax and interface** | Legal encoding, type, schema, ISA, ABI, or protocol form. | Functional behavior, performance, physical feasibility, or system intent. |
| **Functional simulation and testing** | Behavior for exercised stimuli and observed properties. | Unexercised behaviors, physical timing, power, or unspecified security properties. |
| **Formal property and equivalence checks** | A stated property over a modeled transition system, or a stated relation between two artifacts. | Whether the property captures intent, whether assumptions match deployment, or unrelated properties. |
| **Architecture performance and power models** | Quantities represented by the model for the declared workload and configuration. | Effects the abstraction omits or behavior outside its validated region. |
| **Implementation and physical analysis** | Timing, area, power, integrity, or rule results for the modeled design, constraints, modes, and corners. | Missing constraints, unmodeled conditions, functional intent, or manufactured variation outside the analysis. |
| **Post-silicon and operational measurement** | Behavior of sampled parts and systems under measured conditions. | Every manufactured part, workload, environment, lifetime condition, or unmeasured property. |

: **A check is decisive only for the property it observes.** More cost or later
placement in a flow does not widen that property.
{#tbl-check-scope tbl-colwidths="[22,39,39]"}

### Formal Checks and Simulation Make Different Claims

Bounded model checking explores modeled traces through a finite bound \(k\)
under stated assumptions. A beyond-\(k\) result needs an unbounded proof method
such as property-directed reachability, induction, abstraction, composition,
or theorem proving. An unbounded result still proves only the stated property
for the modeled transition system and assumptions.

Equivalence checking asks whether two artifacts preserve a declared relation.
Combinational equivalence compares functions without architectural state.
Sequential equivalence handles state correspondence across time.
Synthesis-oriented flows can account for expected transformations, while
retiming, latency changes, or new state correspondence can make the problem
substantially harder. None of these checks determines whether the original
specification expressed the right behavior. When one model writes both the RTL
and its assertions, the shared omission can sit on both sides of a clean proof
[@FangEtAl2025AssertLLM].

Dynamic simulation samples behavior. Directed tests, constrained-random
stimuli, coverage-guided generation, emulation, formal methods, and
post-silicon testing complement one another because exhaustive simulation is
generally computationally infeasible. Code coverage reports exercised
structures. Functional coverage reports events or bins the verification plan
defined. Neither reports the fraction of every reachable behavior that has
been checked.

The Pentium FDIV case makes the limit concrete. Five missing table entries
escaped pre-silicon testing and produced incorrect results for rare operand
pairs [@Edelman1997PentiumDivision]. Intel later reported a \$475 million pretax
charge for replacement and associated costs [@Intel1995PentiumCharge]. The
case does not show that simulation is useless. It shows that sampled tests
cannot support an unbounded absence claim, and that another check is needed
when a property demands one. Formal verification later became the primary
validation method for the execution cluster in Intel's Core i7 flow
[@KaivolaEtAl2009Corei7Formal].

### Describe the Check Itself

Three questions make a check reviewable.

**Coverage.** Which failures can the check observe, and which relevant failures
leave no signal?

**Possible error direction.** Under the declared model and conditions, is the
result known to be conservative, optimistic, or neither? This must be
established for the particular flow. A pre-route estimate is not always
optimistic, and a deterministic computation is not automatically a safe
bound.

**Shared assumptions.** Which specifications, models, data, workloads,
constraints, code, and tool paths are shared with the producer or with another
check? A different program name or model instance does not create
independence.

@fig-independent-checks contrasts two checking paths. The right side does not
claim perfect independence. It shows how a check that observes the disputed
property through a different path can reduce one known shared failure.

![**A second check adds information only when it changes the relevant failure
path.** A critic using the same assumptions can repeat the producer's omission.
A claim-specific check based on a sufficiently different model or measurement
path can reduce that correlation, but its remaining shared inputs and blind
spots must still be recorded.](images/ch7_independent_checks){#fig-independent-checks
width="92%" fig-alt="Two-column diagram. A producer and
critic sharing the same assumptions lead to correlated agreement. A producer
and a claim-specific check with a different measurement path lead to a
bounded challenge, with remaining shared assumptions explicitly retained."}

Separate teams can fail together on the same hard inputs. Knight and Leveson
found correlated failures among independently developed program versions,
showing that separate implementation does not guarantee independent error
[@KnightLeveson1986Multiversion]. The same warning applies to a generator and
critic that share a foundation model, training data, objective, or
specification. Agreement can be useful corroboration without being an
independent check.

The missing-property case is different. Spectre and Meltdown escaped deployed
verification flows because the relevant information-flow and timing-channel
properties were not adequately observed [@LippEtAl2018Meltdown;
@KocherEtAl2019Spectre]. More functional tests of ordinary program outputs
would not settle confidentiality. Tests designed around leakage can bear on
the security claim, while an ordinary performance suite cannot.

Checks also need checks. Mutation testing injects faults and reports which ones
a suite detects [@DeMilloLiptonSayward1978Hints]. A mutation score says
something only about the injected fault model, and equivalent or unobservable
mutants need careful handling. For AI-authored assertions and testbenches, the
useful fault set should resemble errors the generator actually makes rather
than only traditional hand-written mistakes.

## Proxies Need a Validated Range {#sec-proxy-mismatch-metric-gaming-and-calibration}

An architecture proxy is useful because it is cheaper or earlier than the
quantity that ultimately matters. Estimated IPC, analytical energy, wirelength,
congestion, utilization, and cycle counts can all help order candidates. They
remain partial measurements. The danger grows when an optimizer searches
directly against them, because the search is rewarded for finding every region
where the proxy and the intended result part company.

This is Goodhart's problem in architecture form. A measure that once tracked a
goal can stop tracking it after it becomes the optimization target
[@Goodhart1975MonetaryManagement; @Strathern1997Goodhart]. AI is not unique in
this behavior. It changes the scale and persistence of the search for
loopholes.

@fig-trust-calibration is a conceptual schematic, not a measured curve. Both
axes use normalized quantities. The shaded support region says only where
matched calibration cases exist. Held-out error, ranking stability, and
uncertainty relative to the decision margin determine whether the proxy is
usable even inside that region. Outside it, the relationship is extrapolated
and may diverge.

![**Observed support is necessary but does not establish calibration
accuracy.** The normalized curves illustrate one case where a proxy tracks a
stronger reference over an observed support region and diverges under
continued search. A real study must establish both support coverage and
held-out agreement.](images/F9-trust-calibration){#fig-trust-calibration width="100%"
fig-alt="Conceptual normalized plot. A proxy and stronger reference track in an
observed support region, then may diverge outside it as optimization continues.
A label states that support does not establish held-out agreement."}

Six problems should be tested separately (@tbl-proxy-diagnostics).

| **Concern** | **Diagnostic check** | **What an adverse result means** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Proxy mismatch** | Compare the proxy with a more decision-relevant measurement on matched cases. | The proxy result cannot carry the stronger claim. |
| **Support coverage** | Place matched calibration cases across the workloads and candidate region the search visits. | The reported candidate lies in unsupported extrapolation. |
| **Calibration accuracy** | Measure held-out error, ranking stability, and uncertainty against the decision margin inside the supported region. | The proxy cannot reliably order candidates even without extrapolation. |
| **Confounding** | Hold versions and budgets fixed, use matched contrasts, and test plausible alternative causes. | The difference does not identify the proposed cause. |
| **Variability** | Repeat stochastic flows or sampled workloads and report dispersion or ranking stability. | The point estimate may not resolve the declared margin. |
| **Selection bias** | Re-evaluate the selected candidate on fresh cases not used to choose it. | The apparent margin may contain the luck that made the candidate win. |

: **Each weakness requires a different diagnostic.** A second run cannot repair
a missing property, and a stronger tool cannot repair an unmatched comparator.
{#tbl-proxy-diagnostics tbl-colwidths="[18,43,39]"}

The public debate over learned macro placement illustrates why calibration and
matched comparison matter. Proxy metrics such as wirelength and congestion do
not automatically settle post-route power, performance, and area, and public
assessments have differed in tool flow, baseline strength, pretraining, and
available design data [@ChengEtAl2026UpdatedAssessment]. The durable lesson is
not a verdict on one placement method. It is that a proxy comparison cannot
silently inherit authority from a stronger result obtained under unmatched
conditions.

A simulator can also be the exploited reference. In the architecture-agent
example introduced earlier, a required correctness assertion was absent from
the optimized configuration, so the cycle-level result did not observe the
property credited to it [@GuptaEtAl2026ArchAgent]. Calibration to that run
would reproduce the blind spot. The reference check must itself retain the
property, configuration, and coverage used to justify it.

## Separate the Outcome from the Mechanism

An outcome says what changed. A mechanism says why. They require different
comparisons and can reach different statuses.

For the Lighthouse cache study, the reported outcome question concerns
99th-percentile frame time. The mechanism question asks whether added capacity
reduces capacity misses and whether that reduction explains a tail-latency
change. The 12 percent miss reduction supports the reported intermediate
effect within the cache model. It does not prove that the miss reduction caused
a tail frame-time change. The frame-time interval crosses zero, so the intended
performance outcome remains unresolved.

The reverse can also occur. A candidate may improve the measured outcome while
the proposed explanation fails. The improvement can remain a valid observation
if the comparison is sound, but an unresolved or contradicted mechanism should
not guide the next change. A plausible model explanation is a hypothesis, not
a substitute for a contrast.

Useful mechanism checks include matched workload contrasts, ablations,
counterfactual configurations, traces of the affected events, and sensitivity
around the changed parameter. They should be declared before the result when
possible. Otherwise, an explanation can be fitted to any outcome after the
fact. @tbl-outcome-mechanism keeps the resulting judgments separate.

| **Question** | **Possible status** | **Lighthouse illustration** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Did the requested quantity change in the declared direction?** | Supported, contradicted, or unresolved within the stated comparison. | Tail frame-time improvement remains unresolved because the interval includes zero. |
| **Did the proposed intermediate effect occur?** | Supported, contradicted, unresolved, or not tested. | Capacity misses are reported 12 percent lower for the clean 3\ MB return group. |
| **Did that intermediate effect cause the outcome?** | Supported only by a distinguishing contrast; otherwise unresolved. | The causal link between fewer misses and tail latency remains unresolved. |
| **What did the check not observe?** | Explicit nonclaims. | No result establishes thermal behavior, voltage-droop behavior, functional correctness, security, or system-level XR quality. |

: **Outcome and mechanism remain separate results.** A supported intermediate
effect cannot fill an unresolved architecture comparison.
{#tbl-outcome-mechanism tbl-colwidths="[26,30,44]"}

This separation makes negative results useful. A contradicted mechanism can
improve the architecture model even when the candidate result is favorable. A
resolved regression can rule out a design direction. An unresolved comparison
can reveal that the observation budget or measurement plan was too weak. None
of those outcomes is a failed study if the record keeps them distinct.

## The Lighthouse Scoped Interpretation

The chapter's output is a scoped interpretation rather than a permission or a
design commitment. @tbl-lighthouse-interpretation fills the record for the
constructed cache example.

| **Interpretation field** | **`XR-L2-CAP-A` entry** |
| --- | --- |
| **Source status** | Constructed from an earlier illustrative walkthrough. The values are not live project measurements. |
| **Received execution record** | Three reported `SRAM-A` calls; a clean 2\ MB baseline; one stale-state 3\ MB setup failure; two clean 3\ MB attempts; four cycle-level attempts consumed. Exact inputs, versions, parser status, raw artifacts, frame identifiers, reset state, and attempt-level aggregate attribution are missing. |
| **Candidate and comparator** | `L2-3M-A` against `L2-2M-A`, with workload `XR-TRACE-A` and software `SW-BASE-A` reported as matched. |
| **Reported physical-model checks** | 3\ MB reports 1.4\ mm^2^ area and 2.4\ ns access time, below the 1.5\ mm^2^ and 2.5\ ns dispatch limits. Modeled subsystem power is 2.94\ W, below the 3\ W study limit. These are statements inside the illustration, not independently replayed signoff results. |
| **Reported 4\ MB path** | 1.7\ mm^2^ area and 2.8\ ns access time cross the dispatch limits, and no `SIM-A` call is reported. Accepting the illustrative values as qualified makes 4\ MB a bounded rejection from this study. The incomplete record does not independently verify the parse or dispatch event. |
| **Matched comparison** | The clean 3\ MB group reports 12 percent fewer capacity misses, 2\ mW more cache leakage, and subsystem power increasing from 2.90\ W to 2.94\ W. The producing tool for the leakage difference is unreported. Using baseline minus candidate, the reported 0.3\ ms tail-frame-time reduction has an illustrative 95% interval from -0.1\ ms to 0.7\ ms. Missing frame identities prevent recomputation. |
| **Outcome status** | Unresolved. The reported area, access-time, and modeled-power checks clear their local limits for 3\ MB, but the tail-frame-time interval does not resolve an improvement over 2\ MB. |
| **Intermediate effect** | The clean 3\ MB return group reports fewer capacity misses within the cache model. |
| **Mechanism status** | Unresolved. The record does not establish that the miss reduction caused a tail-frame-time change. |
| **Check limits and nonclaims** | No conclusion about unmodeled physical behavior, functional correctness, security, thermal or power-delivery behavior, full-system XR performance, tapeout readiness, or AI effectiveness. |
| **Required revision** | Start a new bounded study with a complete execution record, a target precision for the tail-latency interval, and a maximum observation budget. Preserve per-attempt artifacts and the contrast needed to test the miss-to-latency mechanism. More samples may narrow sampling error but cannot guarantee a favorable or resolved result. |
| **Reopening conditions** | Reopen after a workload, software, cache-policy, model, tool, PVT assumption, design revision, or stronger contrary observation changes the scope. |

: **A scoped interpretation records both the result and the limit of the
record.** The illustration supports an unresolved performance conclusion and a
reported cache-miss effect, not a resolved causal mechanism or a larger
architecture decision.
{#tbl-lighthouse-interpretation tbl-colwidths="[24,76]"}

The 4\ MB line deserves care. Accepting the illustrative values as given, its
reported area and access time fail the declared checks, so 4\ MB is rejected
from `XR-L2-CAP-A` and no cycle-level call is spent. The surviving record is not
strong enough to independently replay that interpretation because the parser
and dispatch evidence is missing. The bounded rejection also does not apply to
every future study. A new memory compiler, PVT point, area budget, or
access-time target changes the comparison.

The 3\ MB line shows why passing several checks does not settle an architecture
question. The physical-model values meet their local limits. The reported
intermediate effect is favorable. The causal mechanism and intended
tail-latency outcome remain unresolved. Each statement is useful because none
is allowed to impersonate the others.

## Routing Revisions and Reopening Results

A result should change the part of the study that failed. Sending every
adverse outcome back to the generator teaches the wrong lesson and leaves the
real defect in place. A supported result may require no revision at all.
@tbl-revision-routing sends each defect to its owner when a repair is needed.

| **Observed problem** | **Revision destination** | **Reason** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Missing parser status, artifacts, versions, reset state, or attempt lineage | Tool-connected environment | The candidate was not measured with a reconstructable execution record. |
| Candidate state or dependency was represented incorrectly | Design representation | The tool received the wrong design meaning even if it ran cleanly. |
| Comparator, workload, margin, repetition plan, or contrast is inadequate | Study formulation | The comparison cannot answer its declared question. |
| Proxy leaves its validated region or omits a decision-relevant property | Method choice or calibration study | The scoring method no longer supports the ordering being used. |
| A qualified check reports a bounded property failure | Design owner | The candidate or its assumptions need revision within the scope of that check. |
| Outcome is resolved but mechanism is not | Study formulation | Preserve the result while adding a named mechanism contrast before using the explanation to guide another change. |
| Sampling uncertainty leaves the outcome unresolved | Study formulation | Set a target precision, maximum observation budget, and stop rule. More matched samples may narrow sampling error but cannot guarantee resolution. |
| Model bias or proxy mismatch dominates | Method choice or calibration study | Additional repetitions do not repair the wrong abstraction or unsupported ordering. |
| Numerical extraction error or missing execution conditions dominate | Tool-connected environment | The returned value or its scope must be repaired before interpretation. |

: **Repair follows the failed relation.** Execution defects return to the
environment, comparison defects return to the study, and qualified design
failures return to the design.
{#tbl-revision-routing tbl-colwidths="[32,25,43]"}

Reopening does not authorize an action. It marks the conditions under which an
old interpretation no longer applies. A new
workload, software image, tool or model version, operating corner, candidate
revision, calibration result, or contrary observation can reopen a result.
Recording these triggers prevents a bounded comparison from becoming a
permanent fact after its conditions have changed.

The same record distinguishes project learning from model learning. A design
constraint, contradicted comparison, supported intermediate effect, or
supported mechanism can update the project state without becoming
model-training data. A training update needs a named
target, usable labels, scope, and acceptance test of its own. Tool failures,
unmatched results, and unresolved comparisons should not be converted into
simple pass or fail labels.

## Open Research Questions

The open problems begin where current tools stop supplying the interpretation
fields automatically.

**How can a returned field be qualified without hiding unfamiliar failure
modes?** Typed schemas make common quantities easy to compare, while tool and
model changes keep creating warnings and artifacts outside the known schema.

**How can a proxy's validated region be estimated under active search?** The
candidate distribution changes as the optimizer learns where the proxy is most
favorable, which is exactly where previous calibration data may be thinnest.

**How should shared failure sources be measured across checks?** Separate
tools, models, teams, and modalities can still share specifications, workloads,
training data, libraries, or assumptions that create correlated error.

**Which mutations test AI-authored verification collateral?** Traditional
fault models may not resemble the semantic omissions, weak assertions, or
misinterpreted interfaces that generated tests and properties introduce.

**How should scarce high-cost measurements be allocated?** The useful next
check is the one whose possible outcomes can resolve the comparison, narrow
its scope, or distinguish competing mechanisms, not simply the next tool in a
fixed sequence.

**How can credit be assigned without inventing a mechanism?** Long architecture
flows return sparse outcomes after many interacting changes, while localized
diagnostics can be correlated with the proxy that selected the candidate.

**How can partial proofs and sampled measurements compose into one bounded
system claim?** Each check covers a different property and scope, and their
assumptions can overlap or conflict.

## Conclusion {#sec-trust-boundary-conclusion}

::: {.callout-design-principle title="A result is useful only when its limits travel with it"}
A tool return becomes a measurement only after it is bound to a candidate,
quantity, unit, conditions, source, and error. It becomes a comparison only
after a matched comparator and decision margin are added. Its interpretation
must preserve check limits, nonclaims, mechanism status, needed revision, and
reopening conditions.
:::

The central boundary is not probabilistic AI on one side and deterministic
truth on the other. It is the boundary between producing a candidate and
checking a named property through a separate, qualified path. Generators can
be deterministic. Verification tools can be heuristic, randomized, sampled,
or model-dependent. What matters is whether the check observes the property,
under which conditions, with what uncertainty, and with which shared
assumptions.

The Lighthouse example makes the discipline concrete. A stale-state attempt is
an execution failure, not a design measurement. Reported physical-model values
can clear local limits without settling tail performance. A 12 percent miss
reduction can support an intermediate effect inside the cache model while the
causal mechanism and frame-time improvement remain unresolved. Missing
artifacts and conditions remain missing even when the teaching conclusion is
clear.

This chapter therefore hands forward one set of interpretation fields. They
are measurement status, candidate and comparator, quantity and conditions,
difference and uncertainty, check scope and shared assumptions, outcome and
mechanism status, nonclaims, revision destination, and reopening conditions.
@sec-running-the-loop applies those fields to one bounded array-shape study and
keeps a tie, a failed explanation, and a stopping decision separate.
